newsitem.title: USA: San Jose, Calif., bans sitting on sidewalks.
newsitem.headline: San Jose, Calif., bans sitting on sidewalks.

text.p: The city of San Jose, California, has banned people from sitting on downtown sidewalks in a bid to clear the streets of young people and panhandlers, city officials said on Wednesday.

The city council voted 9-to-2 to approve the controversial ordinance, which will take effect in about 45 days, when people will not be permitted to sit on sidewalks in the downtown area between 10 a.m. and midnight. Repeat offenders could be jailed for up to six months and fined up to $1,000.

City officials said the ban was approved in response to complaints by business owners that teenagers and panhandlers were blocking customers and hurting sales in downtown San Jose, about 50 miles (80 km) south of San Francisco.
"There's been a drumbeat of criticism coming from downtown merchants," said Kevin Pursglove, spokesman for San Jose Mayor Susan Hammer.
Advocates for the homeless opposed the measure, saying it unfairly targets the poor.
San Jose officials said their ordinance was modelled after a similar measure in Seattle.
